title: Christopher G. Connell
text:
About
I am a professor in the Department of Mathematics at Indiana University Bloomington. My research centers on differential geometry and its interactions with topology, rigidity, and dynamics. I am especially interested in how curvature, global structure, and dynamical behavior constrain one another.
I also work at the interface of mathematics, computation, and artificial intelligence. I serve as chair of the American Mathematical Society’s Task Force on Artificial Intelligence and the Mathematical Community, and previously served as chair of IU’s Department of Mathematics. My doctorate is from the University of Michigan (1999).

PERSONAL
I am married and the father of seven children, six living. I worship at Trinity Reformed Church in Bloomington, Indiana.

title: Christopher G. Connell
text:
Research
My work is motivated by structural questions in geometry, dynamics, and topology, often connecting global theorems with geometric and analytic methods.


Geometry & rigidity
Curvature, locally symmetric spaces, geodesic flows, and rigidity phenomena, including higher-rank and rank-one settings.


Geometry & topology
Simplicial volume, geometric invariants, and the relationships between geometric structures and topology.


Dynamics & ergodic theory
Geometric dynamics, random walks, and the interplay among invariant structures, flows, and global geometry.


Mathematical AI
Questions at the interface of mathematics and AI, including the use of mathematical structure in computational reasoning and scientific discovery.

title: Christopher G. Connell
text:
Applied mathematics & AI
My applied work has included dynamical network prediction, spectral analysis, integral transforms, and remote sensing. I am interested in moving between mathematical principles and applications in which quantitative modeling can make a concrete difference.
These interests connect with my work in AI and analytics for complex real-world data, including risk and prediction problems.
